newsitem.title: THAILAND: Unocal-led group to start Thai exploration in Nov.
newsitem.headline: Unocal-led group to start Thai exploration in Nov.

text.p: Unocal Corp of U.S. said on Thursday it would start oil and gas exploration in two concession blocks in the Andaman Sea off western Thailand on November 10.
Company spokesman Konthi Kulachol told Reuters that Unocal, in association with France's Total and Statoil, would spend almost US$50 million over the next six years on the project.
The contract to explore the two blocks was signed with the Thai industry ministry on June 19, he said.
Unocal was upbeat about the prospects of finding natural gas in the exploration area. The group will spend $34.3 million during the first exploration phase and $13.8 million in the second phase.
"We hope to find some natural gas in sand stone and carbonate reservoirs in the area...and if we find some, we will consequently sign a production contract," he said.
Water depth in the concession area which covered 48,000 square km, ranged from less than 1,000 feet to more than 3,000 feet, an industry ministry official said.
